what_it_does: Serverless computing lets you run AI inference (asking a language model a question and getting an answer) without managing dedicated servers — the cloud provider spins up a container (a lightweight isolated computing environment) for each request and shuts it down afterward. The downside is a 'cold start': when a new container is launched, it must load the model's billions of numbers from storage into GPU memory, pre-allocate space for the model's working memory (called a KV cache — the running store of context the model builds up while generating a response), and pre-build a library of optimized execution plans for different request sizes. Together these steps add several seconds of delay before the first token can be produced. Medusa sidesteps this by pre-computing and saving all of those initialization artifacts to fast storage during an offline preparation phase, so that a cold-starting container simply loads the pre-built state — much like booting a computer from a hibernation snapshot instead of starting from scratch.
